topic: q-state double-triangular latent causal measurement identification via the explicit local-minor certificate Delta_DT: prove the determinant factorization, K_min(P_X)=K, and a terminating sound-and-complete same-K BLCM reconstruction algorithm A_q modulo coordinate/state relabeling and latent MEC; include the q=3 dense no-pure-child witness and CDM/cdmTools identifiability-check consumer

open_problems.open_problem: For fixed q >= 3, does a q-state double-triangular measurement block have full column rank exactly when an explicit local-minor certificate Delta_DT is nonzero, and does its q^K-by-q^K determinant factor into local q-by-q contrast minors?

source_refs.claim: The binary double-triangular proof obtains full rank automatically, whereas Appendix G gives q=3 failures and requires nonzero degree-(q-1) alternating polynomials for categorical latents.
source_refs.author: Seunghyun Lee and Yuqi Gu

source_refs.claim: Kruskal-based generic identifiability covers broad finite latent structures but does not provide a graph-local determinant certificate for q-state triangular measurement blocks.
source_refs.author: Elizabeth S. Allman, Catherine Matias, and John A. Rhodes

open_problems.why_unsolved: Lee and Gu's binary lemma works because ordinary nondegeneracy forces each binary contrast to be nonzero. For q=3, their Appendix G exhibits triangular conditional tables whose determinant vanishes and identifies alternating-polynomial restrictions not implied by ordinary nondegeneracy. Global Kruskal-rank criteria do not identify which local CPT minors are load-bearing, so the literature supplies neither an explicit Delta_DT factorization nor an exact nonvanishing frontier.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A closed identity expressing the block determinant, up to sign, as a product of explicitly indexed local minors, together with an iff full-rank theorem under Delta_DT != 0 and a zero-factor counterexample establishing the boundary.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation moves from unrealistic pure-child requirements to double triangularity and then isolates categorical latents as the unresolved algebraic boundary.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Pure-child assumptions exclude realistic measurement graphs -> double triangularity identifies binary latent models -> q-state latents break the automatic determinant argument -> an explicit local-minor certificate is required.

method_exemplars.technique: Strategically unfold marginal probability tensors and prove rank dichotomies by factoring conditional-probability matrices; adapt the elimination to triangular rather than pure-item blocks while retaining every exposed local minor.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It turns observable unfolding ranks into constructive graph certificates, the same algebraic interface that Delta_DT must provide.

method_exemplars.technique: Group observables into three conditionally independent views and apply Kruskal uniqueness after proving sufficient factor-matrix Kruskal ranks.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Delta_DT-certified triangular blocks would supply the high-rank views needed to identify latent-state components up to permutation.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct observable Q-matrix goodness-of-fit statistics and derive null limit distributions despite sparse response-pattern tables; replace fit residuals by empirical local-minor residuals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A population polynomial certificate requires a calibrated empirical test before it can support an estimation or software-consumer rung.

open_problems.open_problem: Under positive q-state latent support, double triangularity, and Delta_DT != 0, is the minimal number K_min(P_X) of q-state latent coordinates generating the observed law exactly K, including against lower-dimensional alternatives that need not be double triangular?

source_refs.claim: For binary latents, a rank-2^K observed marginal excludes arbitrary alternatives with fewer coordinates, while categorical full rank is not automatic and is left behind a stronger condition.
source_refs.author: Seunghyun Lee and Yuqi Gu

source_refs.claim: Categorical latent dimensions and state spaces are reconstructed by reduction to a mixture oracle, whose existence is not guaranteed under the minimal nonparametric measurement model.
source_refs.author: Bohdan Kivva, Goutham Rajendran, Pradeep Ravikumar, and Bryon Aragam

open_problems.why_unsolved: The binary rank witness suggests the q-state value q^K, but categorical triangularity alone need not make either conditional table full rank. Kivva et al. recover latent cardinalities only after assuming mixture-component counts. The missing step is therefore a distribution-intrinsic lower bound derived from Delta_DT, with the alternative class stated carefully enough to exclude fewer q-state coordinates without importing a mixture oracle or assuming the alternative is itself double triangular.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem proving K_min(P_X)=K from an observable rank-q^K marginal under Delta_DT != 0, plus a counterexample or separate characterization when alternative latent coordinates may have cardinalities different from q.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames latent causal recovery as jointly learning the unknown number, state spaces, measurement graph, and latent graph.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Latent causal structure is scientifically useful -> its dimension and state spaces are unknown -> a mixture oracle describes information that would suffice -> Delta_DT should make K intrinsic to P_X without that oracle.

method_exemplars.technique: Factor a two-block marginal as M_1 diag(pi) M_2^T and use full column rank of both measurement matrices to force observable rank 2^K; replace 2^K by q^K after establishing Delta_DT.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is the direct dimensional lower-bound argument, with categorical full rank as its only unresolved load-bearing premise.

method_exemplars.technique: Recover latent dimensions from a set function of observed-marginal mixture orders and prove correctness through parent-set combinatorics.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the closest unknown-cardinality reconstruction logic, while Delta_DT would replace its mixture oracle with observed-table ranks.

method_exemplars.technique: Whiten low-order moments, apply robust tensor decomposition, and propagate empirical moment perturbations into component-recovery error bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: An empirical K_min procedure must convert population rank into a stable decision under an explicit smallest-singular-value margin.

open_problems.open_problem: Can observable local-rank and local-minor queries be organized into a terminating algorithm A_q that is sound and complete for reconstructing the q-state double-triangular measurement graph, latent joint law, and latent DAG Markov-equivalence class at fixed K, modulo coordinate and state relabeling?

source_refs.claim: The identification proof uses a rank-2^K CP decomposition, but practical computation is reported as challenging and inaccurate, leading to a penalized-EM-plus-GES substitute without a soundness-and-completeness theorem.
source_refs.author: Seunghyun Lee and Yuqi Gu

source_refs.claim: A constructive tensor-unfolding procedure recovers K and the measurement graph, but requires at least two pure observed variables for every latent coordinate.
source_refs.author: Yuqi Gu

source_refs.claim: Constructive categorical-latent graph recovery is available through a mixture oracle and additional no-twins and maximality assumptions.
source_refs.author: Bohdan Kivva, Goutham Rajendran, Pradeep Ravikumar, and Bryon Aragam

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing results occupy three incomplete corners: Lee and Gu prove population identification for binary double-triangular models but replace the difficult CP step by heuristic estimation; Gu gives an exact rank-query recovery procedure only with two pure indicators per latent; and Kivva et al. handle categorical latents only through a mixture oracle. Targeted searches found no finite q-state, no-pure-child procedure whose branches use observable local minors and whose termination, soundness, and same-K completeness are all proved.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Finite pseudocode A_q with an explicit decreasing search measure and proofs that it terminates on every Delta_DT-certified input, outputs only realizations of P_X, and returns the unique admissible same-K equivalence class modulo coordinate/state relabeling and latent MEC.

writing_exemplar.why: It separates population identification, the CP-decomposition bottleneck, and the heuristic empirical substitute, providing the closest motivation for certified reconstruction.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Double triangularity identifies models without per-latent pure children -> the proof suggests reconstruction -> its CP step is computationally problematic and the implemented substitute is heuristic -> local-minor search should yield a certified A_q.

method_exemplars.technique: Exhaustively unfold population marginal tensors, detect single- and multi-parent structures through exact rank thresholds, and prove that the finite query sequence recovers every measurement-graph row.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest sound constructive graph-recovery proof; A_q must replace its pure-item tests with double-triangular local-minor tests.

method_exemplars.technique: Decompose recovery into bipartite-graph reconstruction, cross-marginal label alignment, latent-law reconstruction, and latent-MEC extraction, with correctness proved module by module.
method_exemplars.why_closest: These modules match A_q's required output, but the new proof must implement them using Delta_DT and observable ranks rather than a mixture oracle.

method_exemplars.technique: Use whitening and robust tensor iterations with a perturbation theorem controlling recovery from empirical moments.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies a concrete estimation rung when exact population minor queries are replaced by noisy empirical tensors.

open_problems.open_problem: Does there exist an explicit q=3, K=3 double-triangular latent causal measurement model in which at least one latent coordinate has no pure child, all latent and measurement probabilities are strictly positive, Delta_DT is nonzero, and the full model is uniquely reconstructible?

source_refs.claim: Binary examples demonstrate identification without pure children, but the categorical appendix instead supplies q=3 determinant-vanishing examples and no dense positive q=3 witness.
source_refs.author: Seunghyun Lee and Yuqi Gu

source_refs.claim: Constructive recovery permits polytomous observed responses but retains finite latent coordinates with pure indicators, leaving the no-pure-child q=3 regime uncovered.
source_refs.author: Yuqi Gu

source_refs.claim: Explicit algebraic identifiability frontiers are established for multiple binary latents, not for q=3 coordinates under double triangularity.
source_refs.author: Yuqi Gu

open_problems.why_unsolved: The q-state extension could otherwise be nonvacuous only on an opaque generic set. Lee and Gu give concrete q=3 triangular parameterizations where the decisive determinant vanishes, while constructive polytomous-response work retains pure indicators. A strictly positive dense witness with an exactly evaluated nonzero certificate is needed to demonstrate that the strengthened condition genuinely reaches the no-pure-child regime motivating double triangularity.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit adjacency matrix and rational q=3 CPTs, with exact evaluations of every Delta_DT factor and a complete reconstruction trace proving uniqueness modulo coordinate/state relabeling and latent MEC.

writing_exemplar.why: Its no-pure-child examples explain the motivating phenomenon, while Appendix G supplies the contrasting ternary failure the witness must overcome.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Real measurement designs may lack pure children -> binary double triangularity can still identify them -> q=3 local determinants can vanish -> a dense positive witness must demonstrate the strengthened certificate's genuine scope.

method_exemplars.technique: Analyze fibers of discrete latent parameterizations through explicit polynomial equalities and construct exact boundary examples separating strict, generic, and failed identification.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The witness requires rational parameter choices and direct polynomial verification rather than an appeal to almost-everywhere genericity.

method_exemplars.technique: Use two triangular blocks to obtain full-rank views, align hidden configurations through recursive partition refinement, recover the measurement graph, and then extract the latent MEC.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A useful q=3 witness must support the entire identification chain, not merely a nonzero isolated determinant.

open_problems.open_problem: Can empirical versions of Delta_DT and the q-state rank certificates yield a calibrated identifiability check that consistently distinguishes certified double-triangular cognitive-diagnosis models from rank-degenerate ones and can serve as a cdmTools-style consumer?

source_refs.claim: Finite-sample CP decomposition was found unsatisfactory, and the implemented alternative uses tuned penalized EM and GES rather than a calibrated test of the identifying certificate.
source_refs.author: Seunghyun Lee and Yuqi Gu

source_refs.claim: The paper derives null limit distributions for goodness-of-fit tests of a provisional Q-matrix, but does not test q-state double-triangular local-minor or latent-dimension certificates.
source_refs.author: Yuqi Gu, Jingchen Liu, Gongjun Xu, and Zhiliang Ying

source_refs.claim: Checkable strict and generic Q-matrix criteria are developed for binary-attribute restricted latent class models and underpin current cdmTools identifiability checks.
source_refs.author: Yuqi Gu and Gongjun Xu

open_problems.why_unsolved: At population level, zero versus nonzero determinant and exact rank are discontinuous decisions. Current Q-matrix tests and cdmTools checks target binary-attribute structural criteria, while Lee and Gu report poor finite-sample behavior for the tensor computation behind their proof. A valid q-state consumer requires a singular-value or local-minor separation margin, simultaneous sampling-error control for every queried marginal, and multiplicity calibration across the reconstruction search.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A computable test based on empirical local minors or smallest singular values, with a null limit law or nonasymptotic concentration bound, familywise calibration over all certificate queries, and uniform consistency away from an explicit Delta_DT margin.

writing_exemplar.why: It formulates identifiability as a checkable decision about a practitioner's proposed Q-matrix and directly motivates the existing cdmTools consumer.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A proposed Q-matrix may not identify the latent model -> checkable graph conditions make the issue operational -> existing software implements binary-attribute criteria -> a calibrated Delta_DT diagnostic should cover q-state double-triangular models.

method_exemplars.technique: Compare observable response moments with restrictions implied by a provisional Q-matrix and derive null limiting distributions for calibrated p-values under high-dimensional response-pattern sparsity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired consumer likewise converts a structural measurement-graph claim into finitely many observable moment restrictions requiring calibrated simultaneous testing.

method_exemplars.technique: Prove tensor perturbation guarantees that propagate empirical moment error through whitening and component decomposition.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its perturbation analysis is a natural template for converting population rank separation into finite-sample recovery guarantees.

method_exemplars.technique: Express measurement-graph membership through exact ranks of strategically selected marginal-tensor unfoldings.
method_exemplars.why_closest: These rank predicates are the closest existing observable certificates to the local-minor predicates the new diagnostic would estimate.

literature_map:
Lee and Gu (2026, TMLR, arXiv:2505.18410) identify binary latent causal measurement models under double triangularity and explicitly call for categorical-latent extensions.
Their Appendix G shows that q=3 triangularity plus ordinary nondegeneracy does not force full rank; degree-(q-1) alternating polynomials must be controlled.
Their binary K theorem excludes arbitrary lower-dimensional alternatives through a rank-2^K marginal, while larger alternatives are excluded only within the double-triangular class.
Their component theorem recovers the measurement graph and, under a nonnested-column condition, the latent law and latent MEC through a rank-2^K CP decomposition.
The same paper reports the population proof's CP step as computationally difficult and empirically inaccurate, substituting penalized EM and GES without a matching completeness guarantee.
Gu (2026, Psychometrika, doi:10.1017/psy.2025.10078) gives constructive tensor-unfolding recovery of K and the measurement graph, but requires two pure indicators per latent coordinate.
Kivva, Rajendran, Ravikumar, and Aragam (2021, NeurIPS, arXiv:2106.15563) reconstruct categorical latent representations and causal graphs through a mixture oracle plus no-twins and maximality assumptions.
Allman, Matias, and Rhodes (2009, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:0809.5032) provide foundational Kruskal generic-identifiability machinery rather than local triangular certificates.
Gu (2025, Bernoulli, arXiv:2203.04403) uses explicit algebraic-fiber analysis to sharpen binary multi-latent identifiability frontiers beyond generic Kruskal conditions.
Gu and Dunson (2023, JRSSB, arXiv:2101.10373) prove identifiable multilayer discrete latent models and posterior consistency under pyramid-specific structure.
Allman, Rhodes, Stanghellini, and Valtorta (2015, Journal of Causal Inference, arXiv:1406.0541) show that hidden discrete Bayesian networks can have ambiguities beyond label swapping, motivating an explicit symmetry statement.
Xu (2017, Annals of Statistics) and Gu and Xu (2020, Annals of Statistics) delimit strict and partial identifiability in binary restricted latent class models, not q-state no-pure-child models.
Gu and Xu (2021, Statistica Sinica, arXiv:1810.03819) give checkable binary Q-matrix criteria used by cdmTools, but those criteria do not cover q-state double triangularity.
Gu, Liu, Xu, and Ying (2018, Psychometrika, doi:10.1007/s11336-018-9629-6) provide a calibrated testing template for provisional Q-matrices; Chen, Liu, Xu, and Ying (2015, JASA) provide an estimation anchor for Q-matrix CDMs.
Targeted searches for q-state double triangularity, explicit local-minor certificates, same-K complete reconstruction, and a cdmTools-style Delta_DT check found no occupied target-method pair beyond Lee and Gu's stated categorical boundary.
prior_proposal_map:
Twenty-one active qid directories were scanned; no bank tree was present in this checkout.
The only proposal-core-like artifact was an interrupted v1 core for stat_pomdp_latent_overlap_minimax.
Its honest_scope exposed shrinking-overlap and uniformly bounded latent-alphabet questions, both centered on POMDP policy-value estimation rather than measurement-model reconstruction.
Its seed_details contained latent-overlap testability and finite-cardinality spectral directions, but their target objects did not coincide with Delta_DT, K_min(P_X), or same-K BLCM recovery.
Its technical_internal_limitation concerned an observed-filtration KL calculation and was also outside the topic anchor.
No proto_core_angle*_rejected.json, rejected proposal TeX, legacy proposal TeX, bank README, or writeup.tex was present.
The panel_ipcw_spectral_ssc_inference and pid_recurrent_capacity_transport_regret review_math.json files contained no topic-relevant strengthening_paths, published_prior_art, or novelty_flags.
Consequently, no Track-A candidate survived topical G1-G4 filtering and no cross-track merge was warranted.
